question: For a basic rural roadside sign, combine Figure 2A-2 with Sections 2A.15 and 2A.16 to state the normal minimum mounting height and lateral offset.
model_answer: Direct Answer: For a basic roadside sign in a rural area, the normal minimum mounting height is 5 feet, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pavement. The normal lateral offset is a minimum of 6 feet measured from the edge of the shoulder, or 12 feet measured from the edge of the traveled way, as depicted in Figure 2A-2; a reduced offset of at least 2 feet is permitted where the normal offset is impractical. Standards (mandatory): - "In rural areas, the minimum height, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pavement, of signs installed at the side of the road shall be 5 feet (see Figure 2A-2)." - For contrast, in business, commercial, or residential areas where parking, bicyclist, or pedestrian movements are likely, "the minimum height... of signs installed at the side of the road shall be 7 feet (see Figure 2A-2)." Guidance (recommended): - The figure note accompanying the standardization-of-location provisions states: "Lateral offset is a minimum of 6 feet measured from the edge of the shoulder, or 12 feet measured from the edge of the traveled way. See Section 2A.16 for lower minimums that may be used in urban areas, or where lateral offset space is limited." Options (permitted): - "On conventional, low-volume rural, and special-purpose roads in areas where it is impractical to locate a sign with the lateral offset prescribed by this Section because of roadside features such as terrain or vegetation, a lateral offset of at least 2 feet may be used." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2A-2 diagrams A and B show a rural roadside sign with "5 ft MIN." height, and lateral offsets of "12 ft MIN." from the traveled way (no shoulder wider than 6 ft) or "6 ft MIN." from the edge of a shoulder wider than 6 feet. - [Image 2] Figure 2A-3 restates in its note that lateral offset is a minimum of 6 feet from the edge of the shoulder or 12 feet from the edge of the traveled way. - [Image 5] shows the full published page containing Figure 2A-2 with the 5-foot height and 12-foot/6-foot lateral offset dimensions for rural roadside signs. - [Image 7] shows Section 2A.15 text (5-foot rural minimum context) and the beginning of Section 2A.16 Lateral Offset. - [Image 8] shows the full published page containing Figure 2A-3 with the 6-to-12-foot lateral offset dimensions at intersections. Citations: - Section 2A.15 Standard §4 (p.58) - Section 2A.15 Standard §5 (p.58) - Section 2A.13 Guidance §6 (p.57) - Section 2A.16 Option §9 (p.60) - Figure 2A-2 (p.51) - Figure 2A-3 (p.52) - Page 92 - Page 100 - Page 93
gold_answer: The minimum mounting height is 5 feet. The normal minimum lateral offset is 12 feet from the edge of the traveled way, or 6 feet from the edge of a shoulder wider than 6 feet.
